title: Clubs and stationary sets: unavoidable subsets of uncountable ordinals

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 61–64 (§14, through Theorem 14.14; uncountability and nonempty closure conditions made explicit)

summary: Closed unbounded sets provide a notion of largeness on regular uncountable ordinals.
abstract: In a regular uncountable ordinal, a closed unbounded set reaches arbitrarily high positions and contains the limits approached by its points. Intersecting fewer sets than the size of the ordinal preserves these properties. A stationary set is unavoidable in the sense that it meets every closed unbounded set, a stronger condition than merely reaching arbitrarily high positions. A diagonal form of intersection preserves closed unboundedness even for a family as large as the ordinal itself.
